thread:
sam: Installed redwoodctl via Homebrew on my M1, but login fails unless I run the binary from /usr/local/bin.
sam: Repro steps:
```
$ which redwoodctl
/opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl
$ redwoodctl login --profile dev
Error: failed to read token cache: permission denied: /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.13.0/libexec/.redwood/tokens.json
```
sam: Weirdly the token file is inside the Cellar and owned by root (created by older installer run with sudo maybe?).
olivia: yikes. mac-arm homebrew path is /opt/homebrew so anything under /usr/local can be a leftover. Can you `stat` the file and show `id -u`?
sam:
```
$ stat -f '%Su %Ol' /usr/local/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.13.0/libexec/.redwood/tokens.json
root  rw-------
$ id -u
501
```
sam: So redwoodctl running as user can't read that file. If I sudo redwoodctl login it works but that's terrible.
ryan: This sounds like two failures: (1) installer wrote default config into Cellar/libexec instead of $HOME, (2) file perms are restrictive. Short-term fix: move the tokens into $HOME and chmod 600. Also check if REDWOOD_CONFIG or REDWOOD_HOME env vars affect lookup.
sam: Tried `mkdir -p ~/.redwood && sudo mv /usr/local/Cellar/.../libexec/.redwood/tokens.json ~/.redwood/ && sudo chown $USER ~/.redwood/tokens.json && chmod 600 ~/.redwood/tokens.json` then `redwoodctl login` works.
olivia: For DX: our client already honours REDWOOD_CONFIG and REDWOOD_TOKENPATH. Document both and the precedence (env overrides $HOME). We should also prefer writing default config at first run into $HOME rather than at build time in the formula.
ryan: Filed devex-bot ticket #4522: "brew formula installs runtime config into Cellar with root perms" and assigned to @ryan. Also adding CI test to verify postinstall creates a per-user default on first run, not in Cellar.
sam: One extra pain: my zsh completion was autoloaded from /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/redwoodctl which autocompletes flags that don't exist on the /opt/homebrew binary. It keeps suggesting --legacy-flag.
olivia: That's a path mismatch issue. Recommend cleaning old completions or `brew unlink redwoodctl && brew install redwoodctl` after removing stale files. We'll also add a note to the M1 troubleshooting doc.
sam: FYI I also hit this from our CI: a macOS runner uses the system-level brew path and the runner user couldn't write to /usr/local/Cellar; tests failed. I changed the CI job to set REDWOOD_CONFIG=$RUNNER_TEMP/.redwood as a workaround.
ryan: Thanks for the CI note. We'll update the brew formula to avoid creating runtime config during package build, and add a postinstall step that creates a user-level scaffold in the user's home only when run as that user (or provide an env var opt-out).
sam: For future: could redwoodctl detect if tokens.json exists in any prefix and warn with a hint to run `redwoodctl doctor`? I almost spent hours chasing PATH.
olivia: Good idea. Add a low-priority enhancement: `redwoodctl doctor` should scan common prefixes (Cellar, /usr/local, /opt/homebrew) and give actionable remediation (chown/move/env var) and mention shell completion locations.
ryan: I'll push a small CLI change to emit a clearer error message when token file is unreadable: include path and a one-line suggested remedy.
devex-bot: created issue #4522: "brew formula writes runtime tokens into Cellar and leaves root-owned file" (assignee: ryan). Please add CI logs and path output.
sam: Thanks all. Workaround in zshrc: `export REDWOOD_CONFIG=$HOME/.redwood` + remove stale completions. Back to green.
olivia: Nice. We'll follow up on the formula and add the doctor improvement to the devex backlog. :white_check_mark:
